definition: The percentage of available production capacity actually used over a period.
formula: KruxOn's actual formula: mean(utilization_pct) across the period (branch 1, 'utilization'/'capacity' match). No numerator/denominator recomputation — the source column is a pre-calculated percentage.
benchmark_note: Higher utilization generally indicates better capacity absorption, but utilization sustained too close to 100% is itself a Lean/TOC (Theory of Constraints) warning sign — it removes the buffer needed to absorb variability without a schedule slip. sub_industry_notes.pharmaceutical: FDA 21 CFR 211's CAPA-timeliness expectation makes this a compliance metric, not just an operational-discipline one — a slow-closing CAPA is itself an audit-findable gap, independent of whether the underlying defect recurs.
sub_industry_notes.automotive: OEM 8D cadence sets the closure clock, not an internal target — Containment (D3) has its own faster deadline than full root-cause closure (D4-D8), so a single 'closure time' figure can mask a fast-contained, slow-closed case.

definition: The financial cost impact of the five most frequent scrap reason codes by unit volume.
formula: KruxOn's actual formula: sum(scrap_units grouped by scrap_reason, top 5 by volume) x avg_unit_cost, where avg_unit_cost = mfg_cost_usd / units_produced when both columns exist, else a hardcoded fallback of $45.50/unit (branch 3). NOTE: the $45.50 fallback is a literal safety default in the code, not a real cost figure — any value shown when mfg_cost_usd or units_produced is missing is using this placeholder, not actual client cost data.
benchmark_note: Pareto analysis (the 80/20 principle) is the standard reason this metric is tracked as a top-5 rather than a full list — a small number of reason codes typically account for most of the cost impact.

definition: Count of process measurements falling outside statistically-derived control limits (not fixed spec limits) — a signal that the process itself has shifted, independent of whether any unit actually failed a spec.
formula: A REAL statistical process control (SPC) calculation, not a keyword placeholder: Individuals control limits via the Moving-Range method (center_line = mean(x), sigma_hat = mean(|x_i - x_i-1|) / 1.128, UCL/LCL = center_line +/- 3*sigma_hat), counting points outside [LCL, UCL]. Implemented in calc_quality.control_limits_i_mr() and calc_quality.spc_chart_data(). Monitors cycle_time_days by default — any numeric process variable in mfg_data can be substituted.
benchmark_note: This is the textbook Individuals/Moving-Range (I-MR) control chart method (Montgomery, Introduction to Statistical Quality Control) — the correct SPC method when measurements come one-per-run rather than in rational subgroups, which is what mfg_data provides.
